_readme: PlayStation Store GraphQL access.
The endpoint accepts ONLY persisted queries whose sha256Hash Sony has
whitelisted: arbitrary GraphQL is refused, and an unknown hash returns
'Query <hash> not whitelisted'. Sony changes a hash when it changes the
query behind it. The one below was published in October 2023 and was
still accepted in September 2026, so this is rare, not routine.
IF THE HASH IS REFUSED, NOTHING BREAKS. GameTracker reads the same price
from the store page instead (store.playstation.com/<locale>/concept/<id>),
which needs no hash, and Settings shows a notice. Updating the hash only
restores the smaller request: a few hundred bytes instead of a ~700 KB page.
WHERE A NEW HASH COMES FROM. Not from your browser: store.playstation.com
never sends this query. Its pages are rendered on Sony's servers, and
metGetPricingDataByConceptId belongs to Sony's other clients (most likely
the PlayStation App). Open-source PlayStation Store libraries publish
these hashes; search GitHub code for 'metGetPricingDataByConceptId' and
take the most recently updated value (github.com/whagency/go-playstation-store
is where this one is published).
TO APPLY IT: copy this file next to your .env, replace sha256Hash below,
then Settings -> Reload keys. No restart needed. That copy wins over the
one built into the app, and the Settings notice clears itself after the
next refresh that gets a price through the query.
